input.question: Which educational institution did Yan Jiao attend?

documents.text: As Dr. Yan Jiao delved into the intricacies of her latest research project, the faint scent of pierogi ruskie wafted through the laboratory, transporting her back to the cobblestone streets of Szczecin, Poland. It was there, at the prestigious Pomeranian Medical University, that her fascination with the human body's mysteries had first taken root. She recalled the crisp autumn mornings, sipping coffee at Café Fregata, surrounded by the soft hum of Polish chatter and the occasional chime of the nearby cathedral. It was during those early days, as a wide-eyed student, that she had stumbled upon the works of Dr. Maria Skłodowska-Curie, whose groundbreaking research had inspired Yan to pursue a career in medicine. As she poured over the latest batch of data, Yan's mind wandered to her favorite professor, Dr. Kowalski, whose passion for anatomy had been contagious. She remembered the way he would gesture animatedly, his bushy eyebrows dancing with excitement, as he lectured on the intricacies of the human brain. It was under his guidance that Yan had honed her skills, eventually earning top honors in her class. The sound of her laboratory door opening broke the spell, and Yan looked up to find her colleague, Dr. Patel, entering with a warm smile. "Yan, I've got the latest results from the trial. You won't believe what we've found," she said, her eyes sparkling with excitement. As they pored over the data together, Yan's thoughts drifted back to those formative years at Pomeranian Medical University, where the seeds of her research had first been sown. The memories, though fond, were bittersweet, reminding her of the long journey that had brought her to this moment. Yet, as she delved deeper into the mysteries of the human body, Yan knew that she owed a debt of gratitude to the institution that had nurtured her passion and set her on this path.
